title: ExtractionScore: A quantitative framework for evaluating synthetic routes on predicted liquid–liquid extraction performance
contribution: A route-scoring metric for computer-aided synthesis planning that accounts for predicted side products and their separability by liquid–liquid extraction (abstract).
problem_entry: CASP tools cannot evaluate reaction selectivity or the effect of side products on purification sequences (abstract).
key_idea: Score a route by predicted side products and their liquid–liquid extraction separability from the major product, via chemical property prediction (abstract).
experiments: Industrially practiced routes to 200 pharmaceutically relevant compounds compared with routes suggested by state-of-the-art CASP software (abstract).
writing: Hedged claim: the metric "may improve" retrosynthetic recommendations (abstract).
transferable: Judge an automated design tool against the solutions industry actually uses (here industrially practiced routes for 200 compounds), not only against other tools (abstract).
coauthors: A. Kuznetsov

quotes.text: We develop a novel quantitative metric called ExtractionScore for evaluating synthetic routes based on the predicted identities of side products as well as the separability of major and side products by liquid–liquid extraction based on chemical property prediction.

title: Decomposition in derivative-free optimization
contribution: A decomposition framework that extends existing DFO solvers (implemented with SNOBFIT) to larger problems, with a convergence analysis and tests on over 300 problems (abstract).
problem_entry: Current DFO solvers do not reach larger-scale problems; scope extension (abstract).
key_idea: Decomposition framework around existing DFO algorithms, implemented with the global model-based solver SNOBFIT (abstract).
proof_devices: Convergence behaviour analysed in the context of global search algorithms; form of the result not stated (abstract)
experiments: Over 300 test problems; for over 90% of problems with more than 75 variables, over 50% objective improvement after 2500 function evaluations, regardless of convexity and smoothness (abstract).
positioning: Relates the framework to superiorization, a methodology from derivative-based feasibility seeking (abstract).
limits_future: Limitations not stated in the abstract (not read).

method_links.note: The group's own DFO method tested later on a large collection (step 7), but the abstract mentions neither certified optima nor a hold-out set.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: decomposition wrapper around an existing DFO solver
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: A decomposition framework wrapped around existing DFO solvers (SNOBFIT) extends them to larger problems.

transferable: Report a wrapper's gain as the share of problems improved by a stated margin at a fixed evaluation budget, split by problem size (abstract).
coauthors: K. Ma, S. Rajagopalan, S. Amaran, S. J. Bury

quotes.text: We show that the proposed framework closely relates to the superiorization methodology that is traditionally used for improving the efficiency of feasibility-seeking algorithms for constrained optimization problems in a derivative-based setting.

Regardless of problem convexity and smoothness, decomposition leads to over 50% improvement in the objective function after 2500 function evaluations for over 90% of our test problems with more than 75 variables.

title: Backward stepwise elimination: Approximation guarantee, a batched GPU algorithm, and empirical investigation
contribution: An approximation guarantee for backward stepwise elimination in best subset selection via approximate supermodularity, a batched GPU implementation, and comparisons with lasso-type and forward methods (abstract).
problem_entry: Best subset selection is NP-hard and costly to solve exactly; practitioners use heuristics without guarantees (abstract).
key_idea: Backward stepwise elimination with an approximation guarantee from approximate supermodularity, plus a batched GPU-parallel version (abstract).
proof_devices: Approximation guarantee via approximate supermodularity, giving conditions for near-optimality or for switching technique (abstract)
experiments: GPU BSE averages up to 5x faster than an efficient CPU version over more than 1.8 million problems; on certain problem classes lower relative test error than the lasso, the relaxed lasso and forward stepwise selection (abstract).
writing: Scoped claim ("For certain classes of problems"); codes and data public on GitHub (abstract).

method_links.note: Subset selection for small models stays the goal and beats the lasso on some classes, but by a greedy heuristic with a guarantee instead of exact integer programming (step 3); listed among the ALAMO publications on minlp.com (metadata).

transferable: Pair a heuristic with a computable guarantee that tells the user when to trust it and when to switch to another method (abstract).
coauthors: B. Sauk

quotes.text: We prove an approximation guarantee for BSE that bounds its performance by applying the concept of approximate supermodularity.
This guarantee provides conditions that suggest the backward stepwise elimination algorithm will return a near-optimal solution, or when another technique should be used.

key_idea: Two hybrid DFO methods that maximise an algorithm's performance after evaluating a small number of configurations (abstract).
experiments: Dense matrix multiplication 1.4x faster than with state-of-the-art autotuners; good parameters within 5% of their effort; any architecture (abstract).

title: Data-driven strategies for extractive distillation unit optimization
contribution: Head-to-head comparison on an Aspen extractive-distillation simulator of surrogate-based optimization (ALAMO vs ReLU networks) and direct black-box optimization (four solvers, three penalty functions); BBO with a smooth penalty works best for the problems studied (abstract).
problem_entry: A fast, dynamic and adaptive way to model and optimize chemical processes, on the energy cost of an extractive distillation process (abstract).
key_idea: Same simulator, two routes: surrogates (ALAMO generalized linear models vs ReLU networks) embedded in math programs, vs BBO directly on simulation results (abstract).
experiments: ALAMO better for the less complex system, ReLU network for the more complex one; BBO with a smooth penalty function the more effective approach for the problems considered (abstract); the CoLab record's highlights add the low-dimensional scope (highlights, CoLab record).
writing: Scoped conclusion ("for problems considered in this study") (abstract).
limits_future: Scope limited to the problems studied (abstract).

method_links.note: Partial: direct BBO beats both surrogate routes, and a ReLU network beats ALAMO's algebraic models on the more complex system; inside Method 3's scope clause (step 1 bars DFO only for discrete designs), and whether this design has discrete decisions is not stated.

transferable: When choosing between surrogate-then-optimize and direct black-box search on a simulator, run both on the same simulator, vary the constraint handling (penalty function) as a factor, and report the winner per system complexity (abstract).
coauthors: K. Ma, R. Bindlish, S. J. Bury, R. Haghpanah, S. Rajagopalan

quotes.text: We find that ALAMO performs well for a less complex system, whereas the ReLU network performs better for a more complex one.
BBO with a smooth penalty function for constraints is the more effective approach for problems considered in this study.

title: Data-driven strategies for optimization of integrated chemical plants
contribution: Surrogate-based operation optimization of an integrated industrial site in a rolling horizon, finding that surrogates at the plant level of abstraction work best (abstract).
problem_entry: Operating a large integrated chemical site is inherently complex, with short-term market change and long-term maintenance plans (abstract).
key_idea: A platform automating simulation and surrogate construction with propagation-error mitigation; surrogates at several abstraction levels inside a deterministic discrete-time optimization model solved in a rolling horizon (abstract).
experiments: Rolling-horizon optimization shows the plant level of abstraction is superior (abstract).
writing: Explicit priority claim ("We are the first to investigate...") (abstract).
limits_future: Guidance: abstract the site network to the level that balances relevant detail with tractability (abstract); the surrogate type is not named in the abstract.

method_links.note: Data-driven surrogates embedded in an algebraic optimization model of an industrial site, with the level of abstraction chosen by experiment; listed among the ALAMO publications on minlp.com (metadata).

transferable: When surrogates feed a site-wide optimization model, treat the level of abstraction of the surrogates as an experimental factor and choose it by the reliability of the optimization results, not by surrogate fit alone (abstract).
coauthors: K. Ma, S. Amaran, R. Bindlish, S. J. Bury, D. Griffith, S. Rajagopalan

quotes.text: We are the first to investigate the impact of different levels of abstraction for surrogate models in site-level optimization.
By optimizing a rolling horizon model with the above optimization model as the underlying model for each planning interval, we show that the plant level of abstraction is the superior approach.

quotes.text: Our present work proposes a novel method based on multiple sequence alignment to explore general patterns among multiple process flowsheets simultaneously without having to conduct pairwise comparisons of a given number of flowsheets.

title: Stochastic analysis and modeling of pharmaceutical screw feeder mass flow rates
contribution: A hybrid deterministic-stochastic screw-feeder model whose errors are captured by an ARMA(2,1) time-series model, replacing slow DEM simulation for process and controller design (abstract).
problem_entry: Flowsheet feeder models give only average flow; DEM models take prohibitively long for realistic high-variance flow (abstract).
key_idea: Time-series analysis and an ARMA model of the non-random variation around a deterministic flowsheet model (abstract).
experiments: Three excipients: leptokurtic, heavy-tailed errors with linear dependence on the prior two seconds; ARMA(2,1) fits with distinct parameters; refilling changes the error distribution, autocorrelation and ARMA parameters (abstract).
limits_future: Groundwork for a broader range of powders and operating conditions (abstract).

method_links.note: A small model fitted to data replaces an expensive simulator, but it is a stochastic time-series model for process and controller design, not an algebraic surrogate for global optimization.

transferable: Instead of moving to a costly particle simulation, model the residuals of a fast deterministic model with a low-order time-series model, check their distribution and autocorrelation, and test whether operating events (here refilling) change them (abstract).
coauthors: B. J. Johnson, M. Sen, J. Hanson, S. García-Muñoz

quotes.text: We propose a hybrid deterministic-stochastic feeder flowsheet model that leverages time series analysis and an Autoregressive Moving Average (ARMA) model to quantify and simulate the observed non-random variation in feeder powder flow.
Furthermore, we show that refilling the feeder online significantly alters the error distribution, autocorrelation structure, and ARMA parameters.

title: Ultrasound-based separation of ethanol-water mixtures is economically advantageous and sustainable
contribution: Experiment-based process simulation, techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessment of commercial-scale ultrasonic ethanol-water separation: over 10% lower annualized cost and over 40% lower CO2-eq emissions (abstract).
problem_entry: The commercial-scale economic and environmental potential of ultrasonic separation is unknown (abstract).
key_idea: Measurements at room pressure, 10-55 °C and 1-5 L/min carrier gas feed process simulations for a data-driven TEA and LCA (abstract).
experiments: Total annualized cost reduced by more than 10% and CO2-eq emissions by more than 40% at commercial scale (abstract).
coauthors: J. W. Ha, J. Liu, H. Feng, H. Seo, J. J. Siirola, J. Na

quotes.text: However, the economic and environmental potential of ultrasonic separation on a commercial scale remains unknown.

Our economic and environmental evaluations show that commercial-scale ultrasonic separation can reduce total annualized cost by more than 10% and CO2-eq emissions by more than 40%, making it a potentially attractive alternative to conventional thermal separation technologies.

contribution: A decade report on BARON: hybrid relaxations, linear and nonlinear presolve, enhanced convexification, heuristics and robustness enhancements, with a benchmark comparison against local and global NLP/MINLP codes (abstract).
problem_entry: BARON has been under development since the early 1990s; the paper documents the features added in the past decade (abstract).

title: Simultaneous convexification for the planar obnoxious facility location problem
contribution: Simultaneous convexification of reverse convex reduced domains gives tighter bounds and optimality-based cuts that certify planar obnoxious facility location instances two orders of magnitude faster than general global solvers, closing 24 open instances (abstract).
problem_entry: Even small instances of this nonconvex QCQP defeat modern global solvers because of weak convex relaxations (abstract).
key_idea: Characterize the simultaneous convex hull of the intersection of reverse convex reduced domains; derive tighter variable bounds and optimality-based cuts with an efficient algorithm; embed in spatial branch-and-bound (abstract).
experiments: Started at an optimal solution, certification two orders of magnitude faster than general-purpose global solvers also started there; without a start, competitive with solvers started at the global solution; 24 open instances certified, 3 improved (abstract).
writing: Priority claim: global optimality certified for the first time for 24 open instances (abstract).
limits_future: Special-class method; on minlp.com's BARON publication list (metadata).

method_links.note: Tighter variable bounds and optimality-based cuts on reduced domains inside spatial branch-and-bound.
A stronger relaxation that comes with an efficient algorithm and is judged by time to certify.
Certified optima for open literature instances, compared under identical starting conditions.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: All solvers are started at the optimal solution so that the comparison measures only the proof of global optimality; the no-start case is reported separately.

transferable: To measure a bounding method, give every solver the same optimal starting solution so the comparison isolates the proof of optimality from the search, then also report the run with no starting point (abstract).
Convexify several reverse convex constraints together, not one at a time, and turn the hull into variable bounds and optimality-based cuts for branch-and-bound (abstract).
coauthors: A. Kuznetsov

quotes.text: Even small instances of this problem are currently beyond the capabilities of modern global optimization solvers, owing to weak convex relaxations.

Given an optimal solution, our approach embedded within a spatial branch-and-bound scheme is able to certify global optimality two orders of magnitude faster compared to state-of-the-art general purpose global optimization solvers also initialized to the optimal solution.

title: A combined linear and nonlinear presolve for nonlinear optimization
contribution: A presolve for nonlinear optimization that combines classical linear presolve with nonlinear reformulations (monotonicity-based fixing, bilinear tightening from linear constraints) while preserving convexity and global optimality, improving one global and four local solvers (abstract).
problem_entry: Presolve gave orders-of-magnitude speedups in LP and MILP; carry it to nonlinear optimization (abstract).
key_idea: Reduce model size and nonlinearity while preserving convexity and global optimality: linear presolve plus reformulation of nonlinear expressions and model simplification (abstract).
experiments: Diverse nonlinear benchmarks and continuous relaxations of discrete nonlinear problems; significant gains for one global and four local NLP solvers (abstract).
limits_future: On minlp.com's BARON publication list (metadata); S083's abstract lists linear and nonlinear presolve among BARON's new features.

method_links.note: Reduction moved into presolve: fixing variables and tightening bilinear products before any search.
Weak: the presolve is part of BARON's documented feature set (S083 abstract; minlp.com list, metadata).

transferable: Test a presolve as a front end for several solvers of both kinds (here one global, four local), so the claim is about the presolve and not about one solver (abstract).
Before the solver starts, fix variables by monotonicity arguments and use the linear constraints to tighten bilinear products (abstract).
coauthors: Y. Zhang

quotes.text: These methods aim to reduce model size and nonlinearity while preserving convexity and ensuring global optimality.
For instance, monotonicity arguments are used to fix nonlinear variables, and linear constraints are exploited to tighten bilinear products.

title: Multiparametric optimization based decision making approach in energy systems planning under uncertainty
contribution: Robust capacity planning with data-driven uncertainty bounds and a bilevel model solved multiparametrically, giving operations as piecewise affine functions of design and uncertainty (abstract of the SSRN preprint version).
problem_entry: Capacity is committed before uncertainty materializes but must stay robust; traditional approaches hedge for the worst case or ignore operational uncertainty (abstract).
key_idea: Robust optimization with probabilistic deep-learning uncertainty bounds and multiparametric solution of the bilevel problem (abstract).
experiments: Multi-source, multi-sink energy system under joint supply-demand uncertainty; capacity shifts to expensive but reliable dispatchables as uncertainty quantiles rise (abstract).
limits_future: The parametric solution allows upfront cost-robustness trade-off exploration (abstract); read version is the SSRN preprint abstract, the journal abstract was not compared.
transferable: Solve the operational lower level multiparametrically so the design-level trade-off (cost against robustness quantile) can be explored without re-optimizing (abstract).
coauthors: H. B. Shah, R. Kakodkar, D. Kenefake, E. N. Pistikopoulos

quotes.text: Traditional approaches either adopt worst-case hedging or ignore operational uncertainty.

We address this through a Robust Optimization framework integrating data-driven uncertainty quantification with multiparametric programming, enabling design strategies as explicit functions of realized uncertainty without iterative re-optimization.
